name: Frankfurt
industries: Banking, central-bank institutions and market infrastructure make Frankfurt continental Europe's financial programme capital.
intro:
Frankfurt runs Europe's monetary plumbing, and its project work carries that weight: the ECB and Bundesbank ecosystem, Deutsche Börse's market infrastructure, and every major global bank's German operation delivering regulatory change on unforgiving deadlines. Post-Brexit relocations thickened the market further. Programme roles here are compliance-bound and formally governed — natural PMP territory — while the fintech cluster and bank digital units hire on agile credentials. Frankfurt professionals work internationally by default, so English-language training fits naturally. Live online batches run year-round with sensible Frankfurt timings — a full Saturday–Sunday weekend cohort plus a midweek Wednesday–Thursday option — so you train during comfortable local daytime hours; the schedule table below lists every upcoming date with its exact Frankfurt start and finish. Afterwards you get precise exam application support, mock exams matching real difficulty, and continued trainer access for questions until you clear.

Frankfurt's project portfolio is denominated in regulation: the banks, the exchange infrastructure and the European institutions clustered here run continuous compliance-driven change, and certified project leadership is effectively table stakes inside those programs. Consultancies serving the financial cluster extend the requirement to their own benches. Training runs live online over two consecutive days in central European hours — no need to cross the Bankenviertel for a classroom. Financial-sector project pay in Frankfurt carries a premium over the German average; the sourced entries in the table below quantify it with named sources. The employer list reflects the banking-and-consulting concentration of demand, and institutions running regulatory portfolios can certify entire change teams via private cohorts.

faq.q: What are the class timings in Frankfurt?
faq.a: Live classes run 09:00 AM – 06:00 PM UK, which is 10:00 AM – 07:00 PM GMT+2 in Frankfurt. You can pick a weekend (Sat–Sun) or a weekday (Wed–Thu) cohort; each completes the course over two consecutive days.

faq.q: Is the training online or at a venue in Frankfurt?
faq.a: All batches are 100% live online, taught by an instructor over video with interactive exercises — there is no venue to travel to in Frankfurt. You need a laptop, a stable connection and a free weekend.

faq.q: Is the certificate different if I attend from Germany?
faq.a: No. The certification is issued by the same global body regardless of where you attend from, and holds identical recognition with employers in Germany and internationally.

faq.q: Can my employer in Frankfurt sponsor the course?
faq.a: Yes. We issue invoices suitable for corporate sponsorship and reimbursement, and most employers in Germany accept them under learning and development budgets. Group pricing is available for teams.
